# Example 15

## Example 15: $((A \wedge \neg \Box A) \rightarrow \Diamond \Box (A \wedge \neg \Box A)) \rightarrow (A \rightarrow \Box A)$ in KT

This is a mouthful, so I'll say a bit more about why it is relevant.

Lots of philosophical views over the years have held the view that **Every truth is knowable**.

## Every truth is knowable

There are a lot of philosophical traditions that have included at least some strands that endorse *Every truth is knowable*.

- **Pragmatism**: Protagorus's dictum "Man is the measure of all things".
- **Idealism**: There is no mind-independent reality.
- **Positivism**: The meaning of a claim is it's verification condition.
- **Scientific Realism**: The scientific method can give us a full picture of the world.

. . .

Do note that in some of these traditions, especially the first and last, there are also plenty of people who deny Every truth is knowable.

## Every truth is knowable

A (relatively) recent objection to *Every truth is knowable* is that if we formulate it in modal logic, it implies the absurd claim *Every truth is known*.

Well, absurd might be too strong; perhaps God knows everything. But still, it would be a striking implication.

## Every truth is knowable

Start by interpreting *Every truth is knowable* as the claim that for any proposition, if it's true, it is possibly known.

So if we interpret $\Box$ as *It is known that*, this sort of means any claim of the form $X \rightarrow \Diamond \Box X$ is true.

The left hand side of 

$$
((A \wedge \neg \Box A) \rightarrow \Diamond \Box (A \wedge \neg \Box A)) \rightarrow (A \rightarrow \Box A)
$$

is an instance of that form, with $X = A \wedge \neg \Box A$.

And the right hand side says, of arbitrary $A$, that if it's true it's known. So in effect this says any truth is known.

---

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, ((A \wedge \neg \Box A) \rightarrow \Diamond \Box (A \wedge \neg \Box A)) \rightarrow (A \rightarrow \Box A)}, checked, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, (A \wedge \neg \Box A) \rightarrow \Diamond \Box (A \wedge \neg \Box A)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, A \rightarrow \Box A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![](../images/tableaux-11/tableau-11-53.tex.svg){width=600px}
:::

Assume the formula is false at world 1. The outer conditional is false, so its antecedent (line 2) is true and its consequent (line 3) is false.

---

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, ((A \wedge \neg \Box A) \rightarrow \Diamond \Box (A \wedge \neg \Box A)) \rightarrow (A \rightarrow \Box A)}, checked, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, (A \wedge \neg \Box A) \rightarrow \Diamond \Box (A \wedge \neg \Box A)}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, A \rightarrow \Box A}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[3]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box A}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[3]}
                    [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Box}[5]}
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![](../images/tableaux-11/tableau-11-54.tex.svg){width=600px}
:::

Line 3 is false: $A \rightarrow \Box A$ is a false conditional, so $A$ is true at 1 (line 4) and $\Box A$ is false at 1 (line 5). False $\Box$ on line 5 introduces world 1.1, where $A$ is false (line 6).

---

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, ((A \wedge \neg \Box A) \rightarrow \Diamond \Box (A \wedge \neg \Box A)) \rightarrow (A \rightarrow \Box A)}, checked, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, (A \wedge \neg \Box A) \rightarrow \Diamond \Box (A \wedge \neg \Box A)}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, A \rightarrow \Box A}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[3]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box A}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[3]}
                    [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Box}[5]}
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1, A \wedge \neg \Box A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\rightarrow}[2]}
                        ]
                        [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Diamond \Box (A \wedge \neg \Box A)}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\rightarrow}[2]}
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![](../images/tableaux-11/tableau-11-55.tex.svg){width=600px}
:::

Line 2 is a true conditional: it branches. Either the antecedent $A \wedge \neg \Box A$ is false at 1 (left branch, line 7), or the consequent $\Diamond \Box(A \wedge \neg \Box A)$ is true at 1 (right branch, line 8).

---

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, ((A \wedge \neg \Box A) \rightarrow \Diamond \Box (A \wedge \neg \Box A)) \rightarrow (A \rightarrow \Box A)}, checked, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, (A \wedge \neg \Box A) \rightarrow \Diamond \Box (A \wedge \neg \Box A)}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, A \rightarrow \Box A}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[3]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box A}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[3]}
                    [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Box}[5]}
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1, A \wedge \neg \Box A}, checked, just = {\TRule{\True}{\rightarrow}[2]}
                            [\sFmla{\False}{1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[7]}, close]
                            [\sFmla{\False}{1, \neg \Box A}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[7]}
                                [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\neg}[8]}, close]
                            ]
                        ]
                        [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Diamond \Box (A \wedge \neg \Box A)}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\rightarrow}[2]}
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]
    ]
]
\end{oltableau}

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
![](../images/tableaux-11/tableau-11-56.tex.svg){width=600px}
:::

\begin{oltableau}
[\sFmla{\False}{1, ((A \wedge \neg \Box A) \rightarrow \Diamond \Box (A \wedge \neg \Box A)) \rightarrow (A \rightarrow \Box A)}, checked, just = \TAss
    [\sFmla{\True}{1, (A \wedge \neg \Box A) \rightarrow \Diamond \Box (A \wedge \neg \Box A)}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
        [\sFmla{\False}{1, A \rightarrow \Box A}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[1]}
            [\sFmla{\True}{1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[3]}
                [\sFmla{\False}{1, \Box A}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\rightarrow}[3]}
                    [\sFmla{\False}{1.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Box}[5]}
                        [\sFmla{\False}{1, A \wedge \neg \Box A}, checked, just = {\TRule{\True}{\rightarrow}[2]}
                            [\sFmla{\False}{1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[7]}, close]
                            [\sFmla{\False}{1, \neg \Box A}, checked, just = {\TRule{\False}{\wedge}[7]}
                                [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Box A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\neg}[8]}, close]
                            ]
                        ]
                        [\sFmla{\True}{1, \Diamond \Box (A \wedge \neg \Box A)}, checked, just = {\TRule{\True}{\rightarrow}[2]}
                            [\sFmla{\True}{1.2, \Box (A \wedge \neg \Box A)}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Diamond}[7]}
                                [\sFmla{\True}{1.2, A \wedge \neg \Box A}, checked, just = {\TRule{\Box}{\text{T}}[10]}
                                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.2, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[11]}
                                        [\sFmla{\True}{1.2, \neg \Box A}, checked, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[11]}
                                            [\sFmla{\False}{1.2, \Box A}, checked, just = {\TRule{\True}{\neg}[13]}
                                                [\sFmla{\False}{1.2.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\False}{\Box}[14]}
                                                    [\sFmla{\True}{1.2.1, A \wedge \neg \Box A}, checked, just = {\TRule{\True}{\Box}[10]}
                                                        [\sFmla{\True}{1.2.1, A}, just = {\TRule{\True}{\wedge}[16]}, close]
                                                    ]
                                                ]
                                            ]
                                        ]
                                    ]
                                ]
                            ]
                        ]
                    ]
                ]
            ]
        ]

]

![](../images/tableaux-11/tableau-11-57.tex.svg){width=400px}

## Upshot

Philosophers who want to endorse *Every truth is knowable* have only two options at this point.

1. Say that somehow in translating their dictum into logic we messed up it's content. And to be fair I have been a bit slippery here with what $\Diamond$ means.
2. Accept the conclusion that *Every truth is known*. This is easy enough if your motivation for this kind of philosophical view is theism. If not...
